Subject: Request: confirmation of immutable in-region residency + deletion evidence for Dedicated

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of TrustBank's procurement security review we need a concise confirmation that for Dedicated deployments: 1) data pinned to an EU region will not be replicated out of-region except for explicit backup/DR paths we agree on; 2) we can obtain time-stamped deletion attestations and forensic logs when a customer-initiated tenant wipe occurs; and 3) a short list of artifacts you can provide to prove deletion (snapshots, tombstone events, KMS key rotations, audit logs).

Can you confirm the precise evidence package you will provide and an estimated delivery timeline? We need enough detail for our internal auditors (SOC/forensics) — ideally an itemized checklist and one sample log.

If helpful, our security engineer (cc'd) can accept SFTP or a secure Drive link for artifacts.

Appreciate it,

Alice Morgan
Head of Cloud Security, TrustBank
alice.morgan@trustbank.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@trustbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:32:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: confirmation of immutable in-region residency + deletion evidence for Dedicated

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear ask. We can provide an evidence package for Dedicated that addresses each of your points. High level:

- Residency guarantee: Dedicated clusters can be pinned to a single EU region. We do not replicate tenant data outside that region unless a documented DR/replication policy is enabled. Backups and snapshots for dedicated customers are *region-local by default*; cross-region replication is an opt-in configuration that requires both parties' sign-off.

- Deletion attestations: For customer-initiated tenant wipes we provide:
  - a time-stamped tombstone entry in our audit log (UTC),
  - a list of snapshot IDs that were expunged or tombstoned,
  - sample KV-cache purge logs,
  - the KMS key rotation and deletion events related to tenant key material (where applicable), and
  - a signed statement from our ops team describing the wipe steps and the retention/hold state at the time of wipe.

- Forensic artifacts: we can include sanitized samples (blinded IDs) of: snapshot manifests, storage object delete logs, IAM events, and the low-level wipe-run log that our agents emit. We cannot share customer data content, but logs and manifests are usable for auditor verification.

I've attached a proposed-evidence-checklist.xlsx that maps each artifact to the auditor question it answers, plus a small backup-replication-map.csv that shows the default replication topology for Dedicated clusters. Monica (privacy) and Laura (legal/ops) are cc'd to confirm any contractual language you need.

Delivery timeline: we can prepare the sanitized package and a single sample log within 5 business days; full runbook + signed attestation within 10 business days. If you need an expedited, certificate-style attestation we can add that as an add-on (shorter timeline with legal sign-off).

Next steps: please confirm the SFTP or secure Drive endpoint you prefer; also let us know if you want logs in CSV or raw text.

Thanks —

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

Quick Q from procurement side (looping in Alice): for backup artifacts — do we provide evidence that backups are tombstoned at storage layer and then garbage-collected per retention TTL, or do we also provide snapshot object hashes that match deletion events? Alice, our standard approach is tombstone + object-delete log + snapshot manifest; auditors sometimes ask for object-level hashes.

Vivek — if we can commit to providing an example snapshot manifest and the corresponding object-delete events (sanitized), that'll check more boxes for banks. If legal is ok with that, I can confirm to Alice today.

— Ben
